Title: Group of Africa's First Ladies during a visit to the Heart and Cancer Centre along with Hospital officials
NewsSummary: The Aga Khan University Hospital welcomed a 12-strong group of Africa's First Ladies to the Heart and Cancer Centre, as part of the 9th Stop Cervical, Breast and Prostate Cancer in Africa (SCCA) Conference programme.
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi welcomed a 12-strong group of Africa's First Ladies to the Heart and Cancer Centre, as part of the 9th Stop Cervical, Breast and Prostate Cancer in Africa Conference programme. 

This year's SCCA Conference, themed 'Investing to Save Lives: The Role of Public-Private Sector Partnerships' was held from July 19-21, 2015 at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre. 

Her Excellency Margaret Kenyatta, First Lady of Kenya - the current chair of the Forum of African First Ladies Against Cervical, Breast and Prostate Cancer, the hosts of the event - and the group were given a tour of the entire facility.

In his welcome remarks, Shawn Bolouki, Chief Executive Officer, AKUH pointed out that the institution is committed to increasing access to those who cannot afford specialised high quality cardiology or oncology care. He showed the guests various sections of the Heart and Cancer Centre which has been functional since July 2011. It is a purpose-built facility with specialised cardiac operating theatres, three ICUs and the latest radiation therapy equipment to treat cancers. 

He noted that non-communicable diseases, including cancer, are becoming a health burden in many countries. An estimated 8 million people succumb to cancer globally every year, with more than 70 per cent of the world's cancer deaths occurring in the developing world and particularly Africa. "Detected early and treated adequately, people with cancer stand a better chance at survival," he said.

As a public service, AKUH organised a free week long cervical, breast and prostate cancer clinic, screening over 1,000 people at the Kenyatta Centre, prior to the Conference.

While delivering the vote of thanks, Dr Saida Rasul, Senior Lecturer, Department of Surgery, Aga Khan University, emphasised the importance of quality treatment: pre-surgery counselling, surgical precision, post-surgical radiation and chemotherapy treatment. Highlighting the substantive participation of AKUH in managing non-communicable diseases such as cancer, Dr Rasul said that competent and compassionate healthcare professionals, state-of-the-art diagnostic equipment, technological tools and treatment protocols that help improve the quality of life for patients are of critical importance in the fight against cancer. 

The 9th SCCA Conference was hosted by the Government of the Republic of Kenya, through the Office of the First Lady and the Ministry of Health, in conjunction with Princess Nikky Breast Cancer Foundation. 

Also present at the Conference were James Macharia, Cabinet Secretary, Ministry of Health and Aly Mawji from the Department of Diplomatic Affairs, Aga Khan Development Network. Speakers of parliaments, ministers for health, diplomats, leaders of organizations and institutions that promote activities to stop cancer, eminent scientists and researchers in cancer, philanthropists, individuals from the private sector, civil society and other stakeholders also attended the Conference.
